gfxReskin.note: MM2's per-vertex skin-blend record. gfxPacket holds a u8 count at +0x24 and a gfxReskin* at +0x28. Size proven three ways - 'shl reg,4; call operator new' at 0x00598AA2 (modModel::LoadAscii) and 0x00599729 (modModel::LoadBinary); the 0x10 stride of the fill loop that follows each ('add ebx,0x10'); and the 0x10 stride of the consumer loop in gfxPacket::Draw(const Matrix44*, uint) at 0x004B371E ('add eax,0x10' per record). The type NAME comes from the linker map: the gfxPacket constructor's 8th parameter is 'class gfxReskin *', and the value passed there is exactly the pointer the caller then stores at packet+0x28. See docs/gfx_layouts.md section 17.

members.name: AdjunctIndex
members.evidence: gfxPacket::Draw 0x004B366B reads byte [rec+0], does 'lea edx,[edx+edx*2]' and indexes the 12-byte-stride transformed-position scratch at 0x0068BCE8 - it selects one already-transformed adjunct to overwrite.

members.name: MatrixGroup
members.evidence: gfxPacket::Draw 0x004B3643 reads byte [rec+1] and uses it as g in packet->MatrixIndices[g+1], which then indexes the caller's Matrix44 palette (shl ecx,6).

members.name: Weight
members.evidence: written at load as __ftol(tokenizer.GetFloat() * 32767.0f) - the constant at 0x005B873C, read out of the file and verified to be exactly 32767.0 - and read at draw as fild + fmul by the constant at 0x005B2A24, verified to be 3.0518509e-05 = 1/32767. Zero-extended on read ('xor edx,edx; mov dx,[eax+2]'), so it is unsigned. modModel::SaveToAscii reads it back the same way at 0x0059A95E.

members.name: Position
members.evidence: the load loop passes &rec[4] to the tokenizer's Vector3 reader (vtable +0x0C); gfxPacket::Draw multiplies [rec+4], [rec+8], [rec+0x0C] against matrix columns 0/1/2 exactly as it does a vertex position.

gfxReskin.file_format: one ASCII line per record: the format string at 0x005DDE54 is '\treskin %5d %3d %6.2f\t%f\t%f\t%f\n' - six conversions for two bytes, one word and three floats, in that order. Its reader keyword 'reskin' is at 0x005DDAB4 / 0x005DDC30. NOTE: modModel::SaveToAscii pushes the raw u16 as an INTEGER against the %6.2f conversion (0x0059A980), a genuine format/argument mismatch in the 1999 exporter. It does not affect the layout and is recorded only so nobody concludes the field is a float.
gfxReskin.semantics: for each record: take palette[MatrixIndices[MatrixGroup+1]], transform Position by it, and lerp the already-transformed position of adjunct AdjunctIndex toward that result by Weight/32767. A fixed-function CPU skin that rewrites entries in the shared scratch buffer, not a second vertex stream.
gfxReskin.header_note: no symbol in the binary is scoped to gfxReskin, so tools/genheaders.py will not emit a gfxreskin.h. Like gfxInterface and gfxResData, it must be hand-written. Merging it here still matters: it is what a hand-written header has to agree with.

verified_unchanged._note: already correct in data/layouts.json. Re-derived here from raw disassembly so nobody 'corrects' them later. merge_layouts.py rule 1 would refuse them anyway.

gfxPacket.now: CONFIRMED - every one of the thirteen offsets, and the size, read off instruction bytes
size_evidence: gfxPacket::Clone (0x004B40F0) at 0x004B4128: 'push 0x2c; call 0x577360' immediately before the copy constructor at 0x004B4170
modModel::LoadAscii at 0x00598BA0: 'push 0x2c; call 0x577360' immediately before the 13-argument constructor at 0x004B38A0
modGetStatic at 0x004A5195: 'push 0x2c; call 0x577360', same pattern - a FOURTH construction site
the 13-argument constructor (0x004B38A0) writes 0x00, 0x08, 0x0C, 0x10, 0x12, 0x14, 0x16, 0x18, 0x1C, 0x20, 0x24, 0x28 and nothing at or beyond 0x2C; 0x04 is written by AllocateVertexBuffer

offset_evidence.0x00: gfxPacket* Next - DrawList (0x004B4870) walks 'mov esi,[esi]'; the copy ctor Clones [src+0] into [dst+0]; modStatic::GetAdjunctCount walks the same chain
offset_evidence.0x04: IDirect3DVertexBuffer7* - AllocateVertexBuffer stores table[i].vb here; DoLock/DoUnlock call its vtable +0x0C (Lock) and +0x10 (Unlock); Draw passes it as DrawIndexedPrimitiveVB's lpd3dVertexBuffer
offset_evidence.0x08: void* - DoLock (0x004B4720) does 'mov eax,[ecx+4]; add ecx,8; push 0; push ecx; push 0; push eax; call [edx+0xC]', so this+8 is Lock's ppbData OUT parameter; DoUnlock (0x004B4740) zeroes it; GetPosition/GetNormal/SetPosition read it on the StartVertex>=0 branch and read 0x0C otherwise
offset_evidence.0x0C: void* Vertices - the system-memory vertex block; sized gfxFVFSize(FVF) * AdjunctCount in the ctor, the copy ctor and CopyFrom; passed as DrawIndexedPrimitive's lpvVertices. On a VB-backed packet this points into the backup at 0x006858E0[i], NOT into the D3D buffer - see gfxPacket::Persist (0x004B45D0)
offset_evidence.0x10: u16 VertexTypeDesc (FVF) - ctor stores arg1 as a word here; every method feeds it to gfxFVFSize/gfxFVFOffset; Draw passes it as DrawIndexedPrimitive's dwVertexTypeDesc
offset_evidence.0x12: i16 StartVertex - SIGNED: the copy ctor (0x004B4180) and CopyFrom (0x004B426C) branch on 'cmp word [x+0x12],0 / jl'; set to 0xFFFF on the system-memory path and to table[i].UsedVerts on the VB path; passed as DrawIndexedPrimitiveVB's dwStartVertex after movsx
offset_evidence.0x14: u16 AdjunctCount - ctor stores arg3; passed as DrawIndexedPrimitive's dwVertexCount; modStatic::GetAdjunctCount (0x004A4DB0) sums word[packet+0x14] over the Next chain, which is where the 1999 NAME comes from
offset_evidence.0x16: u16 IndexCount - passed as DrawIndexedPrimitive's dwIndexCount (0x004B346C); the ctor and copy ctor allocate 2*[0x16] bytes for the index array; modModel::LoadAscii passes 3*tricount ('lea ecx,[edi+edi*2]' at 0x00598C01) into this slot; modStatic::GetTriCount (0x004A4DE0) DIVIDES it by 3 with MSVC's magic-number sequence
offset_evidence.0x18: u16* Indices - allocated and memcpy'd alongside 0x16; GetTri (0x004B3EC0) reads word[[0x18] + i*6 + 0/2/4]
offset_evidence.0x1C: u8* - counted array: ctor allocates arg10+1 bytes, stores arg10 at [0], copies arg11 into [1..arg10]. Draw(Matrix44*,uint) reads [[0x1C] + g + 1] to turn a matrix group into an index into the caller's Matrix44 palette
offset_evidence.0x20: u8* - ctor allocates AdjunctCount bytes and copies arg12 in; Draw indexes it by adjunct number to get the matrix group g used above
offset_evidence.0x24: u8 - ctor zeroes it; both modModel loaders store the reskin count here right after construction ('mov byte [edx+0x24], bl' at 0x00598C38); Draw uses it as the loop bound over the gfxReskin array
offset_evidence.0x28: gfxReskin* - ctor zeroes it; both modModel loaders store the constructor's own 8th argument (typed 'class gfxReskin *' in the linker map) here; Draw treats it as the base of an array of 0x10-byte records

gfxPacket.padding: 0x25-0x27 are compiler padding between the u8 at 0x24 and the pointer at 0x28. Nothing in the binary reads or writes them. code/midtown2/gfx/gfxpacket.h reproduces the object correctly today because natural alignment reinserts the same three bytes.

constructor_arguments._note: 13 stack dwords (ret 0x34). argN is at [ebp + 4 + 4N]. Mapped against the body and against all four call sites; argument 8's declared type 'class gfxReskin *' is what makes the mapping self-checking.
constructor_arguments.2 (+0x0C) unsigned int: NEVER READ. modModel::LoadAscii passes the constant 4.
constructor_arguments.7 (+0x20) unsigned int: NEVER READ by the ctor. It is the reskin count; the callers write [this+0x24] themselves.
constructor_arguments.8 (+0x24) class gfxReskin*: NEVER READ by the ctor. The callers write [this+0x28] themselves. Its declared type is what names gfxReskin.
constructor_arguments.10 (+0x2C) unsigned char: matrix-index count -> [this+0x1C][0]. ALSO the system-memory gate: 0x004B38E1 does 'test al,al / jne' to skip AllocateVertexBuffer when non-zero. A skinned packet must be system memory, so one slot serves both. The gate is NOT argument 13.

gfxPacket.copy_semantics_caution: The copy constructor (0x004B4170) writes 0x00, 0x08, 0x0C, 0x10, 0x12, 0x14, 0x16, 0x18, 0x1C, 0x20 and CopyFrom (0x004B4260) writes 0x04, 0x0C, 0x10, 0x12, 0x14, 0x16, 0x18. NEITHER touches 0x24 or 0x28, so a cloned packet inherits whatever operator new(0x2c) left there. The copy ctor also SHALLOW-copies 0x1C and 0x20 - the clone aliases the original's matrix arrays. Both are 1999 defects, not misreadings. A port with a defaulted or hand-written copy constructor will behave differently, arguably better; record the divergence deliberately rather than reproducing it by accident.
gfxPacket.no_destructor: There is no gfxPacket destructor in the binary or the map. Nothing frees a packet, its vertex block, its index array, its two byte arrays, or its reskin array. Adding a destructor in the port changes observable lifetime.

d3d_vtable_offsets._note: not a class layout. These are the IDirect3DDevice7 and IDirect3DVertexBuffer7 vtable slots the RETAIL draw path calls through lpD3DDev (0x006830C8). An OpenGL device layer that replaces that pointer has to answer at exactly these offsets for as long as any of the surrounding code is still assembly. Five mutually consistent call sites pin them.
d3d_vtable_offsets.IDirect3DDevice7_ordering_trap: The DX7 header order that makes these consistent includes GetClipStatus between SetClipStatus and DrawPrimitiveStrided. Omit it and everything after DrawIndexedPrimitive shifts by four, which makes +0x80 look like ComputeSphereVisibility. It is not: the call at 0x004B337A pushes seven arguments plus this, which is DrawIndexedPrimitiveVB's arity.

IDirect3DVertexBuffer7.+0x0C: Lock - DoLock 0x004B472E, the ctor 0x004B390D, CopyFrom, RestoreAllVertexBuffers

gfxPacket.why: it is not a positions array. DoLock (0x004B4720) passes 'this+8' as the ppbData out-parameter of IDirect3DVertexBuffer7::Lock, and DoUnlock (0x004B4740) writes 0 to it. It holds the mapped base of the shared vertex buffer, valid only between a DoLock and its DoUnlock, and is null at every other time - the constructor sets it to 0 at 0x004B3B47 and never sets it again. GetPosition/GetNormal/SetPosition read it only on the StartVertex>=0 branch, adding gfxFVFSize(FVF)*(StartVertex+i) to it. Treating it as an i32* into positions will read the wrong thing on the first port that dereferences it.

it is a vertex count, not a byte size. The constructor stores arg3 there and separately computes arg3*gfxFVFSize(FVF) as the allocation size; Draw passes it as DrawIndexedPrimitive's dwVertexCount and DrawIndexedPrimitiveVB's dwNumVertices. The 1999 name is fixed by the linker map: modStatic::GetAdjunctCount and modModel::GetAdjunctCount both do nothing but sum word[packet+0x14] over the Next chain. MM2::gfxPacket in the same file already says AdjunctCount; the bare gfxPacket entry does not.

BOTH sources are wrong here and they are wrong in the same direction, so their agreement is not corroboration. FOUR independent proofs. (1) gfxPacket::Draw (0x004B3340) reads it at 0x004B346C and pushes it at 0x004B3475 as the dwIndexCount argument of IDirect3DDevice7::DrawIndexedPrimitive (vtable +0x68, call at 0x004B3491) - the argument position is fixed by the DX7 signature and by the six other arguments around it, all independently identified. (2) The constructor (0x004B3AC2) and copy constructor (0x004B420F) both 'shl eax,1' it and allocate that many bytes for the u16 index array. (3) modModel::LoadAscii computes 'lea ecx,[edi+edi*2]' - three times the triangle count - at 0x00598C01 and passes THAT as the argument the constructor stores here. (4) modStatic::GetTriCount (0x004A4DE0) reads word[packet+0x16] and DIVIDES IT BY 3: the lea chain at 0x004A4DF8-0x004A4E14 evaluates to 21846*n>>16, and 21846/65536 = 0.33333, which is MSVC's magic-number division by three. A triangle count divided by three is not a triangle count. Anyone who sizes an index buffer as 3*[0x16] over-allocates threefold; anyone who loops [0x16] triangles reads three times past the end.

gfxPacket.should_be: u8* MatrixIndices - PROBABLE name, CONFIRMED shape
gfxPacket.why: shape is certain: a counted byte array whose [0] is the count (the constructor allocates arg10+1 bytes, writes arg10 at [0] and arg11 at [1..arg10]) and whose [1+g] is an index into the Matrix44 palette passed to Draw. The name is not recovered - the model file spells the corresponding token 'mtx' (0x005DDAC0), which is a file-format keyword, not a member name, so 'MatrixIndices' is a description.

gfxPacket.should_be: u8* AdjunctMatrixGroups - PROBABLE name, CONFIRMED shape
gfxPacket.why: shape is certain: AdjunctCount bytes, one per adjunct, each a group index that Draw feeds to MatrixIndices. Name not recovered.

both modModel loaders store the reskin record count here immediately after construction ('mov byte [edx+0x24], bl' at 0x00598C38), and Draw(Matrix44*,uint) uses it as the loop bound over the gfxReskin array at 0x28.

the type is wrong, though the width is not. Both modModel loaders store into it the same pointer they pass as the constructor's 8th argument, whose type the linker map spells 'class gfxReskin *'; that pointer is the result of an 'operator new(count << 4)'. Draw walks it in 0x10-byte steps.

gfxMaterial.why: This is the same live error sections 7 and 12 record; round 3 adds a FOURTH and cleanest proof, and it is two-sided. modShader::Load (0x004A3B30) opens 'sub esp,0x48' and its ONLY stack local is a gfxMaterial at the frame's base: 'lea ecx,[ebp-0x48]; call 0x004B1BB0' (gfxMaterial::Reset) at 0x004A3B75. Every [ebp-...] reference in the function is one of -0x48, -0x38, -0x28, -0x18 - the four Vector4 colour members, read off the stream in 0x10-byte chunks. That bounds sizeof(gfxMaterial) <= 0x48 from above; Reset's 'mov dword [ecx+0x44], -1' bounds it >= 0x48 from below. It is exactly 0x48. A fifth, weaker corroboration: modStatic::Draw does 'fld dword [material+0x0C]' to test the diffuse alpha, confirming Vector4 Diffuse at offset 0.
gfxMaterial.caution: this DOES change a size. modShader::AddStaticMaterial (0x004A3930) strides a gfxMaterial pool, so a 0x44 stride there is live corruption, not a cosmetic error. Make the edit deliberately, then rebuild.

phInertialCS.why: docs/port_order.md flags this as a live blocker and calls the two type sources merely 'disputed'. It is not disputed once the bytes are read. phInertialCS::InitArray(phInertialCS* const, int) at 0x00475CB0 strides the array by 0x1B4 three separate ways: 'lea eax,[ecx+0x1b4]' to reach element 1, 'add eax,0x1b4' per loop iteration, and a closing index computation 'lea eax,[esi+esi*2]; lea eax,[eax+eax*8]; lea eax,[esi+eax*4]; lea eax,[ecx+eax*4]' which evaluates to ecx + 436*n. That is the compiler's own array arithmetic on the declared type, so it IS sizeof. It agrees independently with dgRagdoll's operator new(436) and with MM2::phInertialCS. Take the MM2::phInertialCS member list (33 members, 436 bytes), not the bare one, and fix the check_size in the generated header.
phInertialCS.structure_bonus: InitArray also fixes the first three members, which neither source names: [+0x00] is a phInertialCS* Next (element i is given element i+1), [+0x04] is a phInertialCS* Prev (element i is given element i-1), and [+0x08] is a u8 flag the array initialiser zeroes and the default constructor at 0x00475D40 sets to 1.
phInertialCS.caution: this one DOES change a size, so it is the one hand edit here that must be made deliberately and then rebuilt - do not batch it with the gfxPacket renames.

static_data_recovered._note: not class members. These are the free globals gfxPacket's draw and vertex-buffer paths read directly, so an OpenGL device layer has to agree with them at these addresses for as long as any of the surrounding code is still assembly. Names marked (map) come from data/symbols.json; the rest are unsymbolised and are described, not named.
static_data_recovered.0x00684500: bool sm_UseInternal (map) - when true, gfxPacket::Draw(uint) diverts to the internal rasteriser at 0x004B73C0 and gfxPacket::Draw(Matrix44*,uint) returns immediately
static_data_recovered.0x00684501: bool useHWTnL (map) - also gates whether a system-memory backup copy of each vertex buffer is kept (AllocateVertexBuffer 0x004B4500, Persist 0x004B45D3)
static_data_recovered.0x006844F8: bool useNativeVBs (map) - the constructor reaches AllocateVertexBuffer only when this is set AND the 10th constructor argument, the matrix-index count, is zero (0x004B38E1 then 0x004B38E5)
static_data_recovered.0x006857D8: bool gfxForceLVERTEX (map) - selects the constructor's 0x20-stride D3DFVF_LVERTEX (0x1E2) rebuild path at 0x004B3983
static_data_recovered.0x006857E0: the shared vertex-buffer pool, stride 0x10, at most 16 entries (it runs into the array at 0x006858E0). The 1999 name is 'table': the preserved source line at 0x005CD6D4 reads 'lpD3D->CreateVertexBuffer(&desc,&table[i].vb,0)'. Entry layout, read off AllocateVertexBuffer (0x004B43E0) and ReserveVertexBuffer (0x004B4570): +0x00 u32 FVF (the search key), +0x04 IDirect3DVertexBuffer7* vb, +0x08 u32 UsedVerts (bumped by each packet's AdjunctCount; a packet's StartVertex is the value before the bump), +0x0C u32 CapacityVerts (max(4096, AdjunctCount), which is why StartVertex fits in a signed 16-bit field). The entry struct has NO type name anywhere in the binary, so it is described here rather than emitted as a layout.
static_data_recovered.0x006858E0: u8* backups[] - the system-memory copy of each created vertex buffer, indexed by vbtableCount. Written by AllocateVertexBuffer, read by Persist (0x004B45D0) and RestoreAllVertexBuffers (0x004B4690). Persist returns backups[i]+offset, which is what a VB-backed packet stores in Vertices (0x0C) - so Vertices does NOT point into the D3D buffer
static_data_recovered.0x00685CE4: int vbtableCount (map) - indexes 0x006858E0 and 0x006A1CF0, NOT the pool at 0x006857E0
static_data_recovered.0x00685CE8: f32[2048][3] - the transformed-NORMAL scratch buffer, 0x6000 bytes. gfxPacket::Draw(Matrix44*,uint) hands its base to D3D as the strided normal pointer with stride 0x0C
static_data_recovered.0x0068BCE8: f32[2048][3] - the transformed-POSITION scratch buffer, 0x6000 bytes, immediately after the normal buffer; handed to D3D as the strided position pointer with stride 0x0C. Two 2048-adjunct buffers is the hard ceiling on a single skinned packet, and nothing in Draw bounds-checks against it
static_data_recovered.0x00691CE8: int - the number of live entries in the pool at 0x006857E0. Unsymbolised in both sources; distinct from vbtableCount
static_data_recovered.0x00691CF0: the 0x20-stride D3DFVF_LVERTEX scratch array gfxPacket::OrthoMap (0x004B4760) builds and draws with FVF 0x1E2. 0x006A1CF0 - 0x00691CF0 = 0x10000 = 2048 entries. OrthoMap reads the packet's own Vertices with a HARDCODED 0x20 stride rather than calling gfxFVFSize, so it assumes the packet is already LVERTEX
static_data_recovered.0x006A1CF0: IDirect3DVertexBuffer7** vblist (map) - every vertex buffer ever created, drained by FreeAllVertexBuffers (0x004B4640)
static_data_recovered.0x006A3C34: int datCurrentMemoryAlign (map) - set to 4 around every operator new in this subsystem and restored afterwards
static_data_recovered.0x006856A1: RSTATE + 0x01 = gfxRenderStateData::Lighting - gfxPacket::Draw(Matrix44*,uint) reads it at 0x004B3509 to decide whether to transform normals as well as positions

live_draw_call_graph._note: verified by resolving every E8/E9 displacement in .text plus every absolute dword that could be a function pointer. These five functions are the entire retail draw surface above lpD3DDev; section 15 established that gfxPipeline's six draw entry points and the whole vertex-buffer creation path have zero callers.

_corrections_from_first_pass: 0x006844F8 useNativeVBs: the first pass said the constructor takes the AllocateVertexBuffer path 'when this is set and the caller did not ask for a system-memory packet'. The gate is more specific and is worth stating exactly: it is the 10th constructor argument - the matrix-index COUNT - being zero. There is no separate bool. Argument 13, which is declared bool, is never read at all.

gfxReskin Weight: the first pass cited the ASCII writer's '%6.2f' as evidence the field is a scaled float. The writer does use that conversion, but it pushes the raw u16 as an INTEGER (0x0059A980), so the conversion and the argument disagree. The scaling evidence that actually holds is the fmul by 32767.0 at load and by 1/32767 at draw, both constants read out of .rdata and verified.
gfxReskin size: the first pass cited the consumer loop's stride as 'add eax, 0x10' at 0x004B3637. The stride increment is at 0x004B371E; 0x004B3637 is the loop head that reads [this+0x28].
gfxPacket size: the first pass listed three literal allocation sites. There are four - modGetStatic at 0x004A5195 is the one that was missed, and it is the only construction site outside modModel.
